name: design-review
description: Expert design and UX review of rendered web apps, websites, app UI flows, infographics and design artifacts — the last pass before a human looks at AI-built UI. Deterministic accessibility, contrast, target-size, performance, motion and layout-integrity gates first (column alignment, shared rails, section gaps, text overlap, dead space, column/band voids, affordance, token overloading); then structural, state, craft, flow and design-system passes against real renders at multiple viewports; then severity-ranked findings with pasteable fixes, evidence, and an explicit statement of what was never checked. Use this whenever someone asks to review, audit, critique, QA, sanity-check or "give feedback on" a UI, page, screen, flow, prototype, landing page, dashboard, deck or design — or says their UI "looks AI-generated", "looks off", "feels cheap", "needs polish", "isn't accessible", or asks whether something is ready to ship. v1.4.0 closes the four blind spots a real 18-surface review found under a fully green oracle set. The runners now scroll the whole document and drain document.getAnimations() before probing and RECORD what was still running: a gate sampled mid-entrance read a #E85A2A accent as #6a2d18 and reported a surface getting worse after a fix that provably removed its failures, and lazy images probed without scrolling report five of eight as broken. probeColumnVoids() adds the column form of dead space that probeDeadSpace() is structurally blind to — a section that renders nothing still occupies its own margins — plus an unfiltered band-seam table, because a page at 92/205/229px ink-to-ink trips no single threshold and is still three-quarters dead space. probeUnconsumedTokens() catches the token declared, emitted and read by no rule: --primary-on-dark was in the contract, set by every record, present in the DOM and consumed by nothing, so a company's own 72px name sat at 2.14:1. Contrast now reports its denominator, <title> is a Level A gate (two route groups shipped without one), and the parity oracle's landmark set is per-page rather than per-site — a checks=904 diffs=0 green sat over a broken grid row on every index page of every tenant because the oracle only ever loaded /. Also: verify the computed value after a CSS fix rather than the presence of the rule, check WHAT rendered rather than THAT something rendered, and treat any first reading of a time- or scroll-dependent property as provisional.
